rationale: Across published cohorts and case series of biallelic loss-of-function (cysteine-sparing/null) NOTCH3-related small vessel disease and leukoencephalopathy, neuroimaging systematically demonstrates cerebral white matter abnormalities, periventricular leukomalacia-like periatrial volume loss, calcifications, and lacunar infarcts, while consistently sparing the anterior temporal pole white matter. In contrast, involvement of the anterior temporal pole is a classic, established neuroradiological hallmark of dominant CADASIL and is also retained in biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants.

evidence.text: Three pediatric patients with bi-allelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants presented with developmental delay, seizures, cognitive impairment, microcalcifications, and extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities with explicit sparing of the anterior temporal lobes.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: MRI findings pointed at a small vessel disease, with extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, atrophy, lacunes in the basal ganglia, microbleeds, and microcalcifications. The anterior temporal lobes were spared. Bi-allelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants in exons 1, 32, and 33 were found.

numbers.metric: patients with anterior temporal lobe sparing

evidence.text: A proband with a homozygous NOTCH3 null variant (c.2984delC) presented with livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and white matter abnormalities on MRI specifically without anterior temporal pole lesions.

source.title: Distinct neurological phenotypes associated with biallelic loss of NOTCH3 function: evidence for recessive inheritance
source.quote: Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed on a proband who exhibited livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and MRI white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions.

numbers.metric: probands with absent anterior temporal pole lesions

evidence.text: Analysis of 50 patients with biallelic NOTCH3 variants established that biallelic loss-of-function variants produce a distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome with periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia rather than typical CADASIL deep white matter lesions which extend to the anterior temporal lobes.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

new_directions.question_text: Does anterior temporal lobe white matter hyperintensity develop at older adult ages in individuals with biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function variants who survive past childhood?
new_directions.rationale: Most reported biallelic loss-of-function cases have been ascertained in childhood or early adulthood with periatrial leukomalacia patterns; longitudinal neuroimaging past the fifth decade is needed to verify whether temporal pole changes remain strictly absent throughout life.

new_directions.question_text: What is the sensitivity and specificity of temporal pole sparing when differentiating biallelic NOTCH3-related leukoencephalopathy from CARASIL (HTRA1-related recessive arteriopathy)?
new_directions.rationale: CARASIL is an autosomal recessive cerebral small vessel disease that also presents with leukoencephalopathy, alopecia, and spondylosis; identifying whether temporal pole sparing specifically discriminates NOTCH3-LoF from CARASIL is vital for differential diagnosis.
